auditRecords.headline: Ashok Leyland Q1 Results: Net profit rises 2.59% YoY to ₹609 crore, revenue up 10.4%
auditRecords.body: Ashok Leyland reported a net profit of ₹609 crore for Q1 FY27, a 2.59% YoY increase. Revenue grew by 10.4% to ₹9,634 crore, with commercial vehicle volumes hitting a record 48,763 units despite rising material costs affecting operating margins.

auditRecords.headline: S&P assigns investment-grade rating to IDFC FIRST Bank. Can it lift the stock?
auditRecords.body: S&P Global Ratings has assigned IDFC FIRST Bank an inaugural investment-grade rating of BBB- for the long term, with a Stable Outlook. The rating is expected to strengthen the lender’s access to global funding markets and support international operations. S&P also highlighted strong capitalization, improving profitability, stable asset quality and funding.

auditRecords.headline: Natco Pharma Q1 profit falls 57 pc to Rs 206.5 cr
auditRecords.body: Natco Pharma has reported a stark profit decline in the first quarter, largely driven by reduced sales of its leading cancer drug, lenalidomide. This led to a pronounced drop in consolidated revenues compared to the prior year. On a brighter note, the core business showed some positive growth, and total expenses saw a decrease, providing a silver lining to the financial report.

auditRecords.headline: Quest Global said to pick banks for $1 billion India IPO
auditRecords.body: Carlyle-backed Quest Global has appointed five banks for a potential Mumbai IPO targeting up to $1 billion. Axis Capital, Kotak Mahindra Capital, JM Financial, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup will advise. The offering may combine fresh shares and existing investor sales, with a draft prospectus expected by December, though details remain subject to change.

auditRecords.headline: Sensex falls 71 points, Nifty closes below 24,400; broader markets underperform. What lies ahead?
auditRecords.body: The Indian stock market ended lower on Friday as Sensex dropped 71 points and Nifty closed at 24,366. Broader midcap and smallcap indices underperformed, falling 0.7% each. Analysts cite global yield uncertainty and oil prices for the sideways movement, while technical indicators point to key support near 24,200.

auditRecords.headline: Rupee logs weekly decline, with RBI intervention curbing losses
auditRecords.body: The Indian rupee faced a challenging week, depreciating against the dollar amidst mounting tensions from the Middle East conflict. Despite this, central bank interventions and steady dollar sales by state banks helped mitigate more significant losses. With India relying on imports for about ninety percent of its oil, the economy remains susceptible to supply disruptions.
